articles.title: Undertaker Reveals Private Call from Brock Lesnar After WWE Retirement in New Video with Paul Heyman
articles.summary: On the latest episode of his podcast, WWE Hall of Famer The Undertaker revealed that Brock Lesnar contacted him on the day of his retirement match at SummerSlam earlier this month.
articles.body:
On the latest episode of his podcast, WWE Hall of Famer The Undertaker revealed that Brock Lesnar contacted him on the day of his retirement match at SummerSlam earlier this month.

During a discussion with Paul Heyman on Six Feet Under (beginning at the 1:30 mark of the video) , The Undertaker expressed how much it meant to him that Lesnar reached out to him when he did:

"What a full circle kind of moment," The Undertaker said. ... "The phone call that I got yesterday really meant a lot to me. I'm not even gonna get into what the phone call was about, but the fact that I received that phone call, it said a lot about him, you guys together. It was something you didn't have to do, but it meant the world to me as an old-timer.

"I don't think Brock really got enough credit for his passion for the business. ... I think he genuinely—I mean, he had to love this business. And things like that phone call yesterday, just kind of reiterated to me, like, yeah, he understood, he gets it. And it's kind of sad for me because it's one less guy that's gonna be around that understands tradition and the way things used to be done."

Heyman followed up by saying that the phone call was necessary because of the "code of honor" that exists in pro wrestling.

At SummerSlam, Lesnar lost a Hell in a Cell match to Oba Femi and put him over in a huge way afterward by calling him the "future" of WWE. Then, a couple of days later, Lesnar officially announced his retirement from wrestling at the age of 49.

Much like Lesnar elevated Femi at SummerSlam, The Undertaker did the same for Lesnar during the early days of his career.

Taker later gave Lesnar the ultimate rub as well at WrestleMania 30 when Brock ended The Deadman's 21-0 WrestleMania undefeated streak.

While The Undertaker did not get into specifics about what was said when Lesnar called him from SummerSlam, it sounds as though Brock was merely showing his appreciation and gratitude before paying it forward to another up-and-coming star.

articles.title: How the Boston Red Sox finally broke the ‘Curse of the Bambino’ to end an 86-year championship drought
articles.summary: Editor’s note: Watch CNN Original Series “Decades in Sports” on the CNN app. Across six episodes, the series explores the defining moments, athletes and cultural shifts that shaped sports over the past six decades, from the television revolution and Civil Rights Movement of the 1960s, right up to the impact of social media on today’s biggest stars.
articles.body: Editor’s note: Watch CNN Original Series “Decades in Sports” on the CNN app. Across six episodes, the series explores the defining moments, athletes and cultural shifts that shaped sports over the past six decades, from the television revolution and Civil Rights Movement of the 1960s, right up to the impact of social media on today’s biggest stars. For generations, the Boston Red Sox had become accustomed to heartbreak. After winning the World Series in 1918, the famed franchise endured one of the most unprecedented droughts in American sports history. Game 7 losses in 1946, 1967, 1975 and 1986 made it feel as though the Sox might never get over the hump again and lift an elusive sixth Commissioner’s Trophy. By 2004, that barren spell had stretched to a staggering 86 years, reinforcing the idea that Boston was somehow cursed - a notion that had become part of baseball folklore. And when the Sox fell behind 3-0 to the New York Yankees in the American League Championship Series (ALCS), it looked as though history was about to repeat itself. But for a franchise that had spent decades in distress, enough was finally enough. Curse of the Bambino The roots of Boston’s misery stretched all the way back to 1919, when the Red Sox sold Babe Ruth – then a star pitcher and slugger who would become arguably the greatest player in baseball history – to the Yankees. The Yankees then went on to become baseball’s most dominant franchise - winning 27 World Series titles - while the Red Sox would not taste success for the rest of the 20th century. This gave birth to the “Curse of the Bambino,” the notion that Boston’s decision to part ways with Ruth “is the reason why the Red Sox go not only so long without winning a World Series, but losing them in such catastrophic, fateful, cursive ways,” says Devin Gordon, a contributing writer at The New York Times Magazine. After Bill Buckner’s infamous error in Game 6 of the 1986 World Series – with the Sox leading the New York Mets 3-2 in the series and 5-3 in the 10th inning with two outs – it felt as though this cursed team from New England was just destined to always fall short. As CNN Contributor Bob Costas says in the series, “The story of the Red Sox is heartache… so close, yet so far,” and even 2003, Boston’s gut-wrenching loss to the Yankees in Game 7 of the ALCS showed the “Curse of the Bambino” had followed the Sox into the new millennium. So when the two franchises met in the ALCS a year later, it seemed almost inevitable that the Red Sox would come up short again, because as Joe Posnanski – author of Why We Love Baseball – highlights, “hopelessness was probably at a high.” And for good reason, as New York won the first three games to take a commanding 3-0 lead, and as NBC Sports broadcaster Kenny Albert recalls, “in Game 3 it’s not even close, the Yankees score 19 runs (and) they had just demolished the Red Sox.” “I’m a columnist for the Boston Globe, and I destroy these guys in print,” says former Globe columnist Jackie MacMullan. “Their nickname was ‘the idiots,’ and I was like, ‘yeah, they’re idiots alright.’” Game 4 looked certain to be the one where the Sox’ dreams would be crushed by the Yankees once again, as they entered the ninth inning 4-3 down and just three outs away from elimination. One play changed everything But then Boston sent Dave Roberts to first base as a pinch runner, and waiting for him on the mound was Mariano Rivera, arguably the greatest closer in baseball history. Everyone in Yankee Stadium – including Rivera himself - knew Roberts was going to steal, and as Gordon highlights, “it’s very, very hard to steal a base of a pitcher whose one pitch is a 95 mph fastball… which is exactly what happened.” Roberts somehow slid safely into second, and in retrospect, it represented the first crack in the Yankees’ seemingly impenetrable grip on the series. As Posnanski highlights, “It’s not like Dave Roberts’ steal changed anything that was obvious, but looking back on it, you realised it changed everything.” Bill Mueller then drove Roberts home with a game-tying single, before David Ortiz delivered the decisive blow with a walk-off home run in the 12th inning. The Red Sox then won Game 5 in extra innings, went into Yankee Stadium and won Game 6, then returned home for Game 7 and completed the greatest comeback in MLB postseason history, and “it’s pandemonium in Boston like you’ve never seen,” says Gordon. The Red Sox had come back from the depths of despair, then swept aside the St. Louis Cardinals in the World Series to end their 86-year championship drought. And as Posnanski highlights in the series, “it was so perfect because Red Sox fans had built all of this scar tissue around their hearts, and the greatest gift of all that Red Sox team gave them is that once they got to the World Series, they just won, and there was never any pressure that they wouldn’t.” After all those years, the curse had finally been broken, and a franchise once defined by failure suddenly became one of baseball’s great modern success stories. Boston lifted the Commissioner’s Trophy again in 2007, 2013 and 2018, with the Sox’s four World Series titles being the most of any MLB franchise this century. It was one of the greatest turnarounds in American sports history, and it all started with one game - and stolen base - in 2004.

images.caption: Manny Ramirez (center) points out that the Boston Red Sox are No. 1 as players celebrate on the field after their 10-3 victory over the New York Yankees in Game 7 of the American League Championship Series at Yankee Stadium. In an astounding comeback, the Bosox became the first team in baseball history to win a best-of-seven series after losing the first three games. Now, they go on to the World Series.
While playing for the New York Yankees, Babe Ruth became baseball's most prominent player and set many records.
Ramirez stands near the Fenway Park scoreboard showing the New York Yankees winning 17-6 in the seventh inning of Game 3 of the American League Championship Series in Boston in 2004.
Dave Roberts (#31) of the Red Sox steals second base while shortstop Derek Jeter (#2) of the New York Yankees during game four of the ALCS.
David Ortiz celebrates after hitting a two-run home run in the first inning in Game 7 of the ALCS against Yankees.

articles.title: Super League: Warrington Wolves continue winning streak against Huddersfield Giants as Leeds Rhinos rout York Knights
articles.summary: Warrington claimed their fifth consecutive Betfred Super League victory with a 34-24 win against the Huddersfield Giants; Leeds cruised to a 66-16 win over York Knights; the Rhinos are now back at the top of the table
articles.body:
Huddersfield took the lead when Sam Halsall scooped up the ball and went over, but George Flanagan was unable to convert.

Danny Walker replied for the Wire, with Leon Hayes adding the extras to send them in front, and the hosts soon took charge.

In the 28th minute, James Bentley latched onto a quick offload from James Harrison to cross and Sam Powell grounded just two minutes later, with Hayes converting both tries.

Warrington continued to pile on the pressure when George Williams finished off a move down the left flank as they sailed to a 22-4 lead at the break.

After the restart, Halsall scored his second try of the match after holding Adam Clune's kick to cross, with Flanagan converting, but Arron Lindop replied for Warrington and Hayes scored a penalty to extend their advantage further.

Huddersfield continued to apply pressure as Sam Hewitt's try was converted and Connor Wrench then struck after touching down in the corner to close the gap.

Warrington were able to wrap up victory in the last 10 minutes when Matty Ashton grounded and Hayes converted, but the Giants continued to battle until the end when when Jacob Gagai crossed for their fifth try of the afternoon in the final minutes.

Leeds cruise to comprehensive win over York

Leeds returned to the top of Super League after cruising to a comprehensive 66-16 victory over York Knights at the LNER Community Stadium.

Riley Lumb scored three tries and Chris Hankinson added two of his own as well as four conversions as the Rhinos responded instantly to Wigan moving above them on Friday night.

Kallum Watkins, Mikolaj Oledzki, Lachie Miller, Matt Lodge, Ryan Hall, Brodie Croft and Ash Handley were Leeds' other try-scorers, while Jake Connor added another quartet of conversions and Miller one.

Sam Wood, Jon Bennison - who also converted two tries - and David Nofoaluma ensured York would not be shut out.

Lumb had to wait for a review after dotting down in the corner, but his seventh-minute opening try was ultimately confirmed before he acrobatically added his second five minutes later.

Rhinos had taken a 36-0 lead by half-time thanks to Hankinson's first - teed up by Lumb - three minutes later, before Watkins got in on the action, Oledzki added a close-range try and Miller got on the end of Cameron Smith's excellent pass.

Lodge scored his debut try two minutes after the break before Wood finally put points on the board for York. However, Rhinos quickly hit back through Hall ahead of Lumb completing his hat-trick.

Lumb touched down for a fourth time four minutes after the hour as Rhinos kept piling on the points, ensuring two more York tries through Bennison and Nofoaluma counted for little.

articles.title: TNA Lockdown 2026 Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights
articles.summary: TNA's annual Lockdown event has finally arrived, and the company has booked 10  matches inside cages for the show in Chicago.
articles.body:
TNA's annual Lockdown event has finally arrived, and the company has booked 10 matches inside cages for the show in Chicago.

The Hardys vs. The Nemeths (Men's Tag Team Championships)

Allie and TBD vs. The Elegance Brand (Knockout's Tag Team Championships)

Cedric Alexander vs. Leon Slater (X-Division Championship)

The System vs. Fabian Aichner, Ricky Sosa, KC Navarro and Jada Stone

Jason Hotch vs. Mustafa Ali (International Championship)

Xia Brookside vs. Elayna Black (Knockout's World Championship)

Let's take a look at what happened at this year's Lockdown PPV.

The first match on the pre-show saw Vincent and Dutch battle BDE and Rich Swann. BDE and Swann did a choreographed dance during their entrance that did not impress The Righteous one bit.

The size disparity gave Vincent and Dutch a big advantage, and they made sure to use it as much as possible. It didn't take long for this to turn into a pretty physical match, but the crowd wasn't giving them much energy.

The pace eventually slowed, which made the lack of crowd noise much more evident, but all four guys tried their best to get people to pay attention. Things picked up after Swann got the hot tag, but The Righteous were able to score the win in the end.

Result: The Righteous defeated BDE and Swann

The second and final pre-show match saw Special Agent 0 take on Trey Miguel. This was a classic powerhouse vs. high-flyer combo, but Miguel's experience kept him from feeling like an underdog.

Even with a few minor hiccups, their initial exchange helped set the pace for the match. Much like the first match, the usually loud Chicago wrestling audience wasn't giving them much energy. Some fans tried, and there were moments when you could hear more reacting, but it was still unusually quiet most of the time.

Agent 0 put up a good fight, but Miguel ended up scoring the win with a pinning combination similar to a victory roll. They didn't get much time, but they made it count.

There was a couple of audio issues during the pre-show. Matthew Rehwoldt had a funny reaction when his mic had a problem.

The Righteous have such a unique aura and presentation. It's a shame that they haven't found more fame by now, but it's nice to see TNA using them.

The TNA ring being just a bit smaller than the usual WWE ring really stands out once you notice it.

Before coming to TNA, Agent 0 was known as Big Bill Collier, and it's worth taking the time to check out some of his work on the indies.

The cage came down as the pre-show was wrapping up. After the opening video, A.J. Francis made his way to the ring to take on Elijah.

The crowd was chanting for Elijah, but it didn't help him avoid a jumping knee from Francis to kick off the action. The singer recovered and hit a big clothesline before going to the top rope for Walk With Elijah across the top rope.

Francis had a hard time getting in any offense until he was able to send Elijah into the cage wall. From that point forward, it was a back-and-forth fight that saw both men hit some big moves.

Elijah was about to win with a huge Drifter Destroyer, but Expressions interfered and saved Francis. The Drifter spent a little too much time trying to get revenge, allowing Francis to hit his finisher for the win.

These two have been bitter rivals, and they did a good job making this feel like a personal grudge. The pace was a little on the slow side at times, but neither of these guys is known for being fast-paced, so it allowed them to sell everything a bit more than usual.

The fans were noticeably more vocal than during the pre-show, and it definitely helped with the vibe during the match. This was a good choice to start the show because it won't be the match of the night, but it was good enough to wake the crowd up.

During the pre-show, Indi Hartwell had a confrontation with Daria Rae. She said every decision Daria has made has been terrible, and then she made a terrible joke about her name sounding like the word diarrhea.

Chris Bey provided the theme for the show.

The powerbomb Elijah hit while Francis was on the top rope was cool.

Allie and a Mystery Partner vs. The Elegance Brand (Knockouts Tag Team Championships)

With Rosemary out of action, Allie was forced to find a new partner to defend the Knockouts tag titles against Heather and M. The mystery partner ended up being the returning Kiera Hogan, who is a former tag team champion in TNA.

Even though this was a cage match, it was stated that the match would be contested under standard tag team rules, so only one partner was supposed to be in the ring at a time.

Allie took control right away, but she brought in Hogan after a brief exchange to allow the returning star to shine for a bit. Mr. Elegance distracted the champions by climbing on the outside of the cage so his allies could take control.

The energy in this match was high, and you could tell all four women were putting in a good effort, but the way the match was structured prevented it from being as exciting as it could have been. Having normal tag rules in a match that usually has no rules just hampers what they can do.

Heather was small enough to crawl through the cage and retrieve some handcuffs that she used to keep Allie locked to the cage wall, but Kiera was still able to get the pin to help Allie retain the titles.

This match had some bright spots, but it never quite hit its stride. It will be interesting to see is Hogan takes over permanently as a tag champ or if Rosemary will be back soon.

Result: Allie and Hogan defeated The Elegance Brand

The Concierge made some jokes about The Bears leaving Chicago.

It's nice to see Kiera back on TV. It never felt like she got a fair shot in AEW.

It felt like this match would have been exactly the same without the cage. It served almost no purpose here.

The next bout was an Escape the Cage match between Moose and TNA original Frankie Kazarian. Moose had a special entrance with a throne and musicians. As Kaz made his way out, he took a seat in the throne to mock him.

Kazarian tried to escape the cage right away, but Moose kept bringing him back in because he wanted to fight. The big man had a chance to escape through the door, but he chose to lock it instead.

This was a one-sided fight for a long time, but when Moose was about to escape, Kaz gave him two middle fingers and made him angry enough to come back in and make a mistake.

It's hard to pinpoint exactly where the disconnect was, but something about this match didn't work. Both guys were trying, but it never felt like it had the intensity a feud as personal as this one should have.

It certainly had some good moments and spots, but they didn't flow together with the rest of the match. It wasn't until the last couple of minutes that it felt like they found their groove as opponents and really started to make this exciting.

The only way to win was by escaping over the top of the cage or through the door. Both men had a few close calls, but it was Kaz who got the win when Moose knocked him through the door. They telegraphed the finish from a mile away.

The violin and cello players during Moose's entrance were a nice touch.

Kazarian does a good job of making his punches look good. It's an underrated skill in this business.

Rehwoldt calling Moose the world's dumbest fiddle was a funny line.

Moose dropped some F-bombs that were very audible.

The Spanish Fly from the cage that Moose hit was the best spot of the match.

The Knockout's world title was on the line when Xia Brookside stepped inside the cage with Elayna Black, who received a nice reaction from her hometown crowd in Chicago.

Xia talked some trash to the crowd before she and Elayna locked up. They didn't seem to be in a hurry, so both women took some time to taunt each other a few times during their early exchanges.

The pace was much slower than expected, but once Black started bleeding from her head, Brookside started punishing her by using a belt buckle to dig into the wound. It definitely made things feel more brutal.

The match may not have had many exciting moments, but the blood alone made it feel more violent than anything that came before it on the show. Both women clearly wanted this to be a memorable encounter, and they succeeded in that regard.

Black put in a good effort, but Brookeside was able to get the pin and retain her championship. This was booked differently than expected, but that ended up not being a bad thing in the end. Black is definitely going to be remembered for her crimson mask.

The audio picked up all of the trash talk nicely. You could hear everything they were saying.

It looked like Black's head may have hit the cage harder than expected when Brookside dropkicked her into it. It's definitely the moment she started bleeding.

Jason Hotch put his International Championship on the line for the first time on Sunday inside the cage against Mustafa Ali.

Hotch wasted no time going after the man who had made his family's life miserable recently. Ali tried to avoid him, but he ended up with his feet caught in the cage, allowing Hotch to drill him with superkick after superkick.

Within the first two minutes, this immediately became the most exciting match on the show so far. Both guys were bringing all of the aggression you could ask for, and they were moving at a brisk pace to make things even more entertaining.

It took some time, but Ali eventually hit a DDT out of nowhere to turn the tide in his favor. Special Agent 0 took the key from the ref and opened the door for Ali, but Tasha Steelz closed it in his face.

Hotch ended up putting Ali through an announce table with a crossbody from the top of the cage, which was instantly the best spot on the show. Hotch appeared to be bleeding from the mouth after the fall, which led to the ringside doctors tending to him.

Ali took the opportunity to steal a toy from Hotch's daughter at ringside and almost set it on fire before Hotch came into the cage to stop him. Hotch did his best, but Ali won to reclaim the International Championship.

This was an incredibly entertaining match from start to finish.

Ali had a special entrance that involved him carrying a fake Tommy gun to the ring.

Hotch's sit-out powerbomb was really good. The way he and Ali bounced a little on the impact made it look great.

Ali's suicide dive through the cage door to Hotch was awesome.

Hotch hitting a couple of spots from the top of the cage made this the best thing on the entire show.

Cedric Alexander vs. Leon Slater (X Division Championship)

The X Division Championship match between Cedric Alexander and Leon Slater had the added stipulation that if Slater lost, his TNA records would be wiped from existence, meaning his record-breaking reign would no longer be recognized.

As soon as the bell rang, they started trading shots and didn't stop for a long time. Slater was the first one to take control with a couple of running kicks and a hurricanrana from the top rope.

Slater was bleeding from the head after a while, and it really stuck out against Alexander's all-white gear. Since this was also a Last Man Standing match, they never wasted time with pinfall attempts.

They didn't start milking the possible 10-count until later in the match after both men had taken a good amount of damage.

It was going to be hard to match the level of excitement in Ali vs. Hotch, but they did a good job making this bout feel different while still being enjoyable. Alexander and Slater are both very talented, so there was little doubt that this would be good.

Slater stole Alexander's finisher and hit three Lumbar Checks in a row before nailing the swanton 450. Ced was unable to answer the count, which made Slater the winner and new X Division champion.

Avery Styles appeared before this match. He had almost the exact same logo as his dad for the tron. He announced he is officially signed with TNA. Kaz welcomed him to TNA and said he can always trust him.

It will never stop being weird to see Alexander with vampire fangs.

Alexander's Michinoku Driver from the middle rope was great.

The eight-person Lethal Lockdown match was up next. A new competitor entered the ring every two minutes. Once everyone was inside, weapons became available to use. You can't win until everyone is in the ring.

Bear Bronson, Eddie Edwards, Bryan Myers and Alisha Edwards took on Fabian Aichner, Ricky Sosa, KC Navarro and Jada Stone.

The System had the advantage with entries, so they had the numbers advantage multiple times until all eight people were in the match. There were a lot of moving parts in this bout, but they didn't make it too hard to follow.

They had some good moments sprinkled throughout the fight, but it's hard to have this many people in a smaller ring than usual without it feeling overcrowded.

They made good use of the weapons, and we also got a little color during the match, especially from The System, who was able to get the win thanks to Eddie hitting a package piledriver onto some chairs.

This was a fun, violent showdown that picked up quite a bit in the second half.

Elijah was found after an attack backstage, but nobody knows who did it.

Navarro's dive through the door looked cool.

Stone's moonsault from the top of the cage was cool, but she basically landed standing up, and that could not have been fun for everyone to catch.

The Hardys vs. The Nemeths (Tag Team Championships)

Unlike the Knockouts tag title bout, this match was contested under tornado tag rules, so Matt and Jeff Hardy, Nic and Ryan Nemeth were all in the ring at the same time to fight for the men's tag belts.

Early in the match, Nic and Ryan both tried to escape the cage even though that was not a way they could win under these rules.

Nic and the Hardys are all veterans, and Ryan is by no means a rookie, so they were able to put together a decent show that played into their strengths as individuals and teams.

A table was brought into the ring, but it took them a long time to make use of it. Matt put Ryan through it with an elbow drop from the wall of the cage, but that didn't end the match.

Nic ended up htting his finisher on Matt to get the win in a moment that seemed to catch most of the crowd off guard. Several fans were shown looking baffled by the outcome.

Most of the match was fine, but the way it ended clearly left a bad taste in the mouths of many in attendance. Slater came out at the end and said his legacy in the X Division has been cemented, and he has one more goal. He challenged Nic to a world title match and handed his belt over to Carlos Silva.

The announcers pointed out that is Nic won, he would be the first person to hold the world and tag titles at the same time in 20 years.

Matt looked like he might have gotten injured early on, but he recovered quickly.

The return of TNA Lockdown was a bit of a mixed bag, but the night wasn't without its highlights.

Black and Brookside had a war that was as bloody as it was fun, Elijah and Francis put on a good show, and Slater regained the X Division title only to turn it over for a world title shot at Bound for Glory.

However, the highlight of the night was Ali vs. Hotch. Those two delivered a match that blew everything else on the show out of the water.

Avery Styles joining TNA is going to be met with mixed reactions online, but until we see what he can do, we won't know what his chances are.

The show was a tight three hours, and while some matches definitely left a lot of room for improvement, the good ones were enough to carry the PPV.

articles.title: Beau Greaves: 'Beau and Arrow' defeats Lisa Ashton and Aileen de Graaf to close in on her 60th title on the Women's Series circuit
articles.summary: After missing out on Saturday's action, darting sensation Beau Greaves returns to the Women's Series with a bang as the Doncaster star wins back-to-back titles on Sunday to claim her 58th and 59th titles on the Women's Series circuit
articles.body:
Sunday's Women's Series double-header saw Events 19 and 20 take place at the Matiolli Arena, as Greaves returned to winning ways on the circuit after missing yesterday's action.

Greaves opened her account Sunday morning with three consecutive whitewash victories over Jane Hawtin, Sue Lowther and Vicky Pruim respectively

The 22-year-old was almost denied a 58th Women's Series title, as she fought back from 3-2 down to beat Gemma Hayter to book her spot in the quarter-final stage.

Greaves raced into the semi-final, as she beat Aileen de Graaf 5-1 with an average of over 96, before booking her place in the Event 19 showpiece as she raced past Kirsty Hutchinson 5-2.

In a repeat bout of the 2025 Women's World Matchplay semi-final between 'Beau 'n' Arrow' and Lisa Ashton, it was Greaves' who came out victor in the final as she beat Ashton 5-3.

Despite dropping the opening leg in the final, Greaves responded with three legs of her own in quick succession to gain a two-leg advantage on Ashton, before sealing the victory with a brilliant 14-dart leg.

Greaves opened her Event 20 campaign in the same manner as she did earlier in the day, winning back-to-back matches in quick succession, beating Leanne Halls and Felicia Bay 4-0.

The Doncaster star - who only dropped three legs in the entire event - won consecutive matches 4-1 over Louise Pearson and Rhian O'Sullivan respectively, before dispatching Angela Kirkwood 5-0 to seal her spot in the final four.

There, she raced into the final, as Greaves beat Karolina Ratajska 5-1, opening her account in that match with a brilliant 11-dart leg.

De Graaf's below-par performance in the final meant that Greaves was victorious once again and claimed her 59th Women's Series, averaging upwards of 91 and whitewashing the Dutchwoman.

Greaves remains on top of the Women's Series rankings, with Ashton and Sherrock solidifying their positions in second and third respectively, as Hayter sits just behind the pair in fourth spot and in the final qualification spot for the 2026/27 World Darts Championship.

The top three players from the final PDC Women's Series rankings will qualify to compete in the 2026/27 Paddy Power World Darts Championship, with the top-ranked player also qualifying for the 2026 Mr Vegas Grand Slam of Darts.

articles.title: Salah scores two goals, has two disallowed in first start for Trabzonspor
articles.summary: Salah started his first game for the Turkish Super Lig side, whom he joined on a free transfer earlier this month.
articles.body:
Mohamed Salah ‌‌opened his account in the Turkish ⁠⁠Super Lig ⁠⁠with a double as Trabzonspor beat Istanbul Basaksehir 2-1 to clinch their first win ⁠⁠of the season.

Salah, who joined Trabzonspor on a free transfer after leaving Liverpool ⁠⁠following a trophy-laden nine-year spell, also had two goals disallowed in a standout performance on Sunday.

Making his first league start after appearing as a substitute in Trabzonspor’s ‌‌season opener, Salah put his side ahead in the eighth minute, capitalising after Basaksehir goalkeeper Muhammed Sengezer failed to hold on to the ball.

Basaksehir’s Eldor Shomurodov equalised from the penalty spot in the 19th minute, but Salah restored ⁠⁠Trabzonspor’s lead three minutes into the ⁠⁠second half, bursting down the right, exchanging passes with Ernest Muci and slotting the ball into the far corner.

The 34-year-old ⁠⁠winger had a stoppage-time effort chalked off for a foul in ⁠⁠the build-up and another ruled ⁠⁠out for offside when he found the empty net from long range with the goalkeeper upfield for a corner.

He will ‌‌now turn his attention to Thursday’s Europa League playoff second leg away to Ferencvaros after his ‌‌side ‌‌suffered a 1-0 home defeat in the first leg.

articles.title: Mercedes no longer have the fastest car in F1, says leader Antonelli
articles.summary: McLaren’s reigning champion Lando Norris celebrates his second win in a row from pole position at Zandvoort.
articles.body:
McLaren have taken a big step forward and Mercedes no longer have the quickest car in Formula One, championship leader Kimi Antonelli said after the Dutch Grand Prix.

McLaren’s reigning champion Lando Norris celebrated his second win in a row from pole position at Zandvoort on Sunday, with Antonelli and Mercedes teammate George Russell finishing second and third, ahead of Ferrari pair Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc.

list 1 of 4 ‘Simply lovely’: Verstappen extends with F1 Red Bull Racing until 2030

list 2 of 4 Norris finally wins a race in 2026 with Hungarian Grand Prix triumph

list 3 of 4 Formula One returns to Malaysia as Sepang circuit hosts Bahrain Grand Prix

list 4 of 4 F1 needs better balance between business and sport, says Norris

“We’re clearly not the fastest car any more on the grid,” said Antonelli, who won five races in a row earlier in the season.

“We’re probably second or third, at least in today’s race, and McLaren has taken a huge step, especially since Hungary, since the big upgrade package they brought.”

However, Norris, who lost out to Antonelli at the race restart and then had to overtake him on track, questioned that assertion.

“I don’t think it’s true. I think if I didn’t get Kimi when I overtook him, I don’t think I would have won the race,” he said.

“For once, I would give myself a little bit of credit that I feel like I’m doing a better job than everyone, and I think that can also make a difference.

“We certainly have a car now capable of beating them … but I think they have a better all-round performing car than what we do.”

Zandvoort, and Budapest’s Hungaroring before that, played to McLaren’s strengths but some of the tracks coming up may be less favourable.

Ferrari can be expected to go well at their home Grand Prix at Monza early next month, with upgrades in the pipeline, while Antonelli faces hefty grid penalties for an engine change.

Mercedes are still way ahead of Ferrari and McLaren in the constructors’ championship and scored more points – 46 to McLaren’s 43 and Ferrari’s 31 – than anyone else over the weekend.

“We have a strong car in certain areas. It’s not like last year where we were pretty good everywhere,” said Norris.

“We’re very, very strong in high speed, and that’s the place we’ve improved the car the most, is high-speed performance. No one matches us in high speed, and that’s a good thing.

“But the advantage that they [Mercedes] have to us in slow speed is also crazy. And therefore, I don’t have the confidence to say ‘yeah, I can easily fight for a championship for the rest of the season’.”

“I know I’ve just won two races in a row and had two poles in a row, but at the minute I don’t have the car I need to fight for a championship,” added the Briton, who is 83 points behind Antonelli, with 11 rounds remaining unless the situation in the Middle East forces a calendar change.

Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said cost cap restrictions meant Mercedes did not have the money to implement developments on the car as quickly as they might want.

“We are trying to evenly split that through the season based on our calculations of when we can bring the biggest updates and optimising the championship points,” he told reporters.

“So the ride has been a bit tougher than at the beginning of the year.”

McLaren principal Andrea Stella said he expected Mercedes to accelerate their car’s development regardless.

“I’m sure their car in the wind tunnel is quite a bit faster than the car they have on track,” said the Italian.

“And they will want to now convert some of this potential into upgrades that make it to the real car. I’m just pretty sure that they will have upgrades.”

Antonelli will take grid penalty at home race

Antonelli, who turns 20 on Tuesday, faces another obstacle in his quest to become F1’s youngest-ever champion.

He will need to take a hefty grid penalty at his home Italian Grand Prix in two weeks as Mercedes plan to swap his car’s power unit to head off potential reliability problems in the second half of the season. That will put Antonelli over his allowance of key components for the year.

“Our theory, our calculations say that that’s the best track to take it. Obviously, our algorithms don’t take the nationality into consideration,” Wolff said. “We’re here to fight for a championship and not the most PR, so that’s what we’re going to do.”

Monza is a high-speed track where the Mercedes engine is likely to be strong, and overtaking is relatively easy, giving Antonelli a chance to make up places. He has accepted the decision.

“I think it still will give me a chance to do a great result and bring home good points,” he said.

articles.title: Give Imran Khan proper medical care, cricket legends urge Pakistani gov’t
articles.summary: Twenty-one cricket captains request PM Sharif’s government to ensure Khan is given timely and independent medical care.
articles.body:
Pakistan’s imprisoned former prime minister and cricket captain, Imran Khan, must be given “humane treatment and proper medical care”, urge a group of cricket greats in a letter seen by Al Jazeera and addressed to Pakistan’s current Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

Twenty-one former captains from around the world have appealed to Sharif’s government to allow an independent assessment of Khan’s health, reinstate his weekly family visits and provide him with the required medical treatment without delay, four signatories of the letter confirmed to Al Jazeera late on Sunday.

Khan, 73, has been imprisoned for the past three years on a range of charges.

On Tuesday , Pakistan’s Supreme Court ordered local authorities to transfer Khan from Adiala jail to the privately run Shifa International Hospital by midnight on Thursday. However on Saturday, Khan’s party, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), filed a contempt petition against the government after he was sent to a state-run hospital instead of the private facility ordered by the top court, party officials said.

Khan is widely regarded as one of the world’s greatest-ever all-rounders and arguably Pakistan’s greatest cricketer, who led his nation to its first World Cup win in 1992 and holds the record for most international wins for a Pakistani captain.

Khan’s former cricket adversaries turned friends said the recent events prompted them to pen a letter to Sharif, who replaced the PTI founder as prime minister in April 2022 and again after Pakistan’s last general election in February 2024.

The letter, dated August 23, follows similar outreach in February by 14 former international cricket captains who raised concerns over Khan’s deteriorating health and alleged mistreatment during his imprisonment.

“We wrote then not as politicians, but as former colleagues and rivals who share a bond forged on the cricket field — one that transcends the borders and disputes that too often divide countries,” said the letter.

“We write again now — joined by seven further former captains — because of what has reportedly just occurred,” read the letter, whose signatories include cricket Hall of Famers Sunil Gavaskar, Kapil Dev, Clive Lloyd, Allan Border, Greg Chappell, Ian Chappell, John Wright and David Gower.

Greg Chappell, who shared a friendly bond with Khan following their retirement from cricket, initiated the letter on both occasions.

Lloyd told Al Jazeera on Sunday that he contributed to the letter. Former England captains David Gower, Nasser Hussain and Michael Atherton also confirmed signing it.

Notably, no former Pakistani cricketers were among the signatories of both letters, although several star players have publicly voiced concerns over Khan’s health in the past.

Gavaskar, Dev and Dilip Vengsarkar are the three Indian players among the 21, while former Sri Lanka captain, Arjuna Ranatunga, is the other South Asian name.

Former Australian women’s team captains Alex Blackwell and Belinda Clark are also on the list of signatories.

The letter praised the “welcome steps” of the Supreme Court ordering Khan’s transfer to a private hospital for medical examination by a board that included personal physicians and his sister, Dr Uzma Khan.

The signatories requested the government that:

The medical board directed by the Supreme Court — including Khan’s own doctors — be permitted to complete a full and independent assessment of his health, particularly the reported loss of vision in his right eye.

The weekly family visits reinstated by the court be honoured without interruption or administrative delay.

Whatever the outcome of that medical assessment, the treatment recommended by it be provided without delay.

The former cricketers lamented Khan’s short-lived hospital visit. They reiterated the concerns raised by his family, who said the examination by a state-appointed team and swift return after being declared “medically fit” fell short of what the Supreme Court ordered.

“Whatever the legal and political arguments surrounding his case, the basic decency of ensuring a court-ordered medical process is actually completed is not, in our view, a controversial request,” the letter said.

“It is one we believe every nation that plays this game would recognise as fair.”

The Pakistan government did not respond to Al Jazeera’s request for a comment.

Full list of signatories: Michael Atherton, Alex Blackwell, Allan Border, Michael Brearley, Greg Chappell, Ian Chappell, Belinda Clark, Alastair Cook, Sunil Gavaskar, Lee Germon, Adam Gilchrist, David Gower, Kim Hughes, Nasser Hussain, Clive Lloyd, Kapil Dev Nikhanj, Deshamanya Arjuna Ranatunga, Sir Andrew Strauss, Dilip Vengsarkar, Stephen Waugh, John Wright.

Chappell praises Khan’s charisma and power

Following the first appeal made to the Pakistani government in February, Greg Chappell wrote and spoke about his bond with Khan and what prompted him to take the lead in writing the letter.

He said that the letter was meant to highlight a human rights issue rather than be a political intervention and admitted being pleasantly surprised at how quickly it came together since everyone was in the same boat.

“This seems to have had some real impact,” Chappell said as he emphasised the need for the first letter to have “long-lasting impact” rather than fizzle out in the next news cycle.

The former Australian captain praised the charisma Khan wielded both on the field as a cricketer and later when he entered politics.

“People were threatened by someone like Imran because of his aura, personal power and charm,” he told the Cricket Et Al podcast in February.

“They were threatened by him and obviously that’s played its part in this.”

images.caption: Twenty-one former cricket captains have raised concerns over Khan’s deteriorating health and alleged mistreatment during his imprisonment [File: KM Chaudary/AP Photo]
Imran Khan’s sister Uzma, with his personal physician Faisal Sultan speaks to reporters in Islamabad, August 21, 2026 [Anjum Naveed/AP]

articles.title: BS Meter on Dylan Larkin, Cutter Gauthier and the Latest NHL Trade Rumors
articles.summary: The dog days of the NHL off-season continue as August draws to a close.
articles.body:
The dog days of the NHL off-season continue as August draws to a close.

Following a frenzy of activity in the trade market within the first two days of July, business has slowed to a crawl. Only five trades have occurred since July 2 , all involving minor-league players.

However, trade activity could pick up once the calendar flips to September. With training camps opening in mid-month and the regular season beginning on Sept. 29 , NHL general managers could soon start shopping around to address any lingering roster issues.

Meanwhile, the media rumor mill continues churning over potential moves involving some key players.

Some, such as Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin, have previously surfaced in trade rumors this summer. Others, like Calgary Flames defenseman Zach Whitecloud, have started popping up as trade candidates.

Follow along as we dust off our BS Meter to separate fact from fiction regarding the latest NHL trade chatter.

Montréal Canadiens Have 2 'Sign-and-Trade' Candidates

With September and the start of training camp fast approaching, the Montréal Canadiens have not yet re-signed defenseman Arber Xhekaj and winger Zachary Bolduc. The two depth players are restricted free agents coming off low-cost contracts and should be affordable re-signings for the Canadiens.

Stu Cowan of The Montreal Gazette speculated about whether Xhekaj and Bolduc still have futures with the Canadiens. Because they haven't re-signed yet, he concluded that they could be part of a sign-and-trade scenario.

The Canadiens still require a second-line center. Cowan pointed out that general manager Kent Hughes hasn't ruled out making a trade in September or October, adding that he wouldn't make a "dumb trade" for a quick fix.

Given the young talent within the Canadiens system, there might not be room for Xhekaj and Bolduc. They could be pushed out if one or two of their promising players crack the lineup during training camp.

Sign-and-trade scenarios usually happen with stars or second-tier talent, not low-cost depth players. Both could draw attention if available in the trade market. However, even in a package deal, they won't fetch the second-line center the Canadiens require without adding a significant sweetener.

Darcy Kuemper and Trevor Moore Could Be Los Angeles Kings' Trade Candidates

The Los Angeles Kings made several roster changes during this offseason.

Long-time captain Anze Kopitar retired, and Andrei Kuzmenko and Mathieu Joseph departed via free agency. Mats Zuccarello and Erik Haula arrived via free agency. So did Corey Perry, back for a second stint after joining them last season.

Nevertheless, Kings general manager Ken Holland might not be done tinkering with his lineup this season. Ryan O'Hara of The Hockey News suggested goaltender Darcy Kuemper and winger Trevor Moore as trade candidates .

Kuemper, 36, was a Vezina Trophy finalist with the Kings in 2024-25. However, he struggled last season after an injury, which cost him the starter's job to Anton Forsberg. If he can't regain that spot, the Kings might attempt to move him and his $5.3 million cap hit .

O'Hara complimented Moore's speed and ability, but noted the 31-year-old winger hasn't cracked the Kings' top-six forward lines full-time. He carries a $4.2 million annual cap hit through 2027-28 , and scored a career-high 31 goals in 2022-23.

Both players could be trade chips to address other roster issues for the Kings. Kuemper could draw interest from teams seeking an experienced starting goalie, while Moore could entice clubs that are in the market for a skillful middle-six winger.

Calgary Flames Could Trade Zach Whitecloud

The Calgary Flames have rebuilt their roster over the last two seasons by trading veterans for draft picks, prospects, and younger players.

They're expected to be sellers this season if they're out of playoff contention by the March 1 trade deadline.

Zach Whitecloud is currently the Flames' biggest trade chip. Acquired from the Vegas Golden Knights in January, the 29-year-old is a reliable defenseman with Stanley Cup experience. He has two years left on his contract with an affordable AAV of $2.8 million.

Kent Wilson of the Calgary Sun believes the Flames will retain Whitecloud this season to provide experience and leadership to their young defense corps. However, he doesn't rule out a trade if young blueliners Simon Nemec and Zayne Parekh step up this season.

Some observers still consider Whitecloud a suitable trade target this summer for clubs seeking a skillful, experienced top-four defenseman with a right-handed shot. The Toronto Maple Leafs and Montreal Canadiens have been suggested as suitors.

The Flames could move Whitecloud if their young defensemen show improvement this season. However, those promising youngsters will likely need another season to develop, meaning they'll need a seasoned hand like Whitecloud to help them.

Anaheim Ducks Could Make Cost-Cutting Trade to Sign Cutter Gauthier

The Anaheim Ducks were caught by surprise when center Leo Carlsson signed a five-year contract offer with the Philadelphia Flyers worth an average annual value of $18 million.

The Ducks matched the offer, but it left them with insufficient salary cap space to re-sign Cutter Gauthier.

A restricted free agent coming off an entry-level contract, Gauthier led the Ducks last season with 41 goals and 69 points. The 21-year-old winger reportedly rejected a four-year contract offer from the Ducks worth $14 million annually.

With $9.07 million in salary cap space , the Ducks must shed salary once Gauthier is signed. They'll get some short-term salary-cap relief by placing sidelined winger Troy Terry ($7 million AAV) on long-term injury reserve, but they must be cap-compliant when he's ready to return to the lineup.

Andre Leal of The Hockey News believes the Ducks must make a couple of cost-cutting trades . He suggested wingers Alex Killorn ($6.25 million AAV), Chris Kreider ($6.5 million), and Frank Vatrano ($4.6 million) as likely trade candidates.

If Gauthier has rejected $14 million annually, he won't accept anything within the Ducks' current remaining cap space. The Ducks are a rising team in the Western Conference and cannot afford to lose their leading goal scorer. Killorn, Kreider or Vatrano could be playing elsewhere later this season.

Minnesota Wild Can't Afford to Acquire Dylan Larkin

In early June, it was first reported that Dylan Larkin requested a trade. That made the 30-year-old Detroit Red Wings center a fixture in the rumor mill and appeared in our August NHL Trade Targets list.

Larkin has a full no-movement clause, but is reportedly willing to waive it for the Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights, Florida Panthers, and Dallas Stars.

According to MLive.com's Ansar Khan, the Wild were his preferred landing spot , but they might be unable to meet the Wings' asking price.

Khan stated the Red Wings sought, at minimum, a top-six forward (preferably a center) in return for Larkin. However, the Wild aren't parting with that type of asset, and Khan indicated the Red Wings aren't interested in a return of futures such as draft picks and prospects.

Wild followers aren't optimistic about their club's chances of landing Larkin. In a fan poll earlier this month by Michael Russo and Joe Smith of The Athletic, 68 percent of respondents didn't believe their team could acquire him, citing the club's limited trade capital.

The Wild don't have a top-six forward to spare, and their lack of a true first-line center is the reason they were linked to Larkin in the first place. Unless the Wings lower their price, the Wild must get creative, perhaps by getting a third team involved that has the assets that could interest Detroit.

articles.title: Ranking the 5 Most Likely Men's WWE Money in the Bank 2026 Winners
articles.summary: Sunday Night's Main Event is the next big show for WWE on September 6, but the next official premium live event is Money in the Bank on October 10.
articles.body:
Sunday Night's Main Event is the next big show for WWE on September 6, but the next official premium live event is Money in the Bank on October 10.

The MITB event is usually one of the more anticipated PLEs on the calendar because the outcome isn't always as predictable as the average match. Plus, who doesn't love a good fight with ladders?

There are a lot of potential names who could end up in this year's men's Money in the Bank bout, but only a handful seem like possible winners.

Let's take a look at some of the most likely names to walk out of New Orleans with the briefcase.

Royce Keys has had slightly inconsistent booking lately, but it's clear WWE management sees him as a potential top star.

He might be new to the company, but the 17-year veteran is by no means a rookie, so it would make perfect sense for him to end up in this match.

The only thing that kept us from placing him higher on the list is the fact that he has not won a title in WWE yet, and it might be best to give him a run with the United States or Intercontinental Championship to see how he does.

Keys winning would immediately inject some new blood into the main event scene, which WWE sorely needs right now.

Finn Balor has talked a lot about wanting to get back into the hunt for a world title since coming to SmackDown, and this might be his way back into the chase.

Balor was the first-ever universal champion, but an injury during the title match in which he won the belt forced him to relinquish it before he ever got to defend it.

Now that he is free from The Judgment Day and back to his old babyface ways, it would be the perfect time to throw him into the title picture.

His popularity has been consistent, and Balor has always been a reliable performer in the ring, so there would be no downside to giving him the briefcase at this stage in his career.

Drew McIntyre has been out of action since losing to Jacob Fatu at WrestleMania 42, but if he is ready to come back, this would be the perfect time.

The MITB briefcase would make him even more dangerous than he already is, which is saying a lot because he is one of the most physically imposing members on the WWE roster.

Whether the Scot does it as a heel or babyface doesn't matter because his return would be cheered by fans either way, so WWE has some wiggle room with the kind of story it would tell with him holding the case.

The only downside to this scenario is that McIntyre won the briefcase in 2024, so having him repeat so soon might not be the best option.

WWE NXT Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights Before Heatwave 2026

Trick Williams is currently involved in a feud with Baron Corbin over the United States Championship, but once that is done, it wouldn't be surprising to see WWE test him out in the main event scene.

It's no secret that WWE sees Trick as a valued member of the roster. He is booked strong, featured regularly and has a celebrity manager. His ascension has been quick but steady.

Putting the MITB briefcase in his hands would not be a bad idea at all. Even if he didn't successfully cash it in, having him circling the world title picture would be a great next step in his career.

If he ends up being booked in the match, we're giving him strong odds to win.

Solo Sikoa is definitely going to end up challenging Roman Reigns for the world title at some point, but he would be so much more dangerous with the MITB briefcase.

This would be a slam-dunk decision for WWE. Sikoa has built real momentum with the WWE Universe in recent months, and now is the time to capitalize.

Having him use the briefcase to defeat Reigns would also protect The Tribal Chief's character, which is something WWE seems intent on doing.

A few months of Sikoa parading around with the briefcase and taunting his cousin with it before finally cashing it in would be highly entertaining television.

Do we actually think Danhausen will win the Money in the Bank match? No, but there is an argument for why it would be great.

The beauty of his character is he is not driven by the same motivations as every other pro wrestler. Titles don't seem to be his top priority, so there is an easy comedic avenue to take.

Imagine Danhausen wins the case and then opens it to find a contract when he was expecting human monies. He would be the first person in WWE history to be mad about winning, but he could take advantage of the situation.

Having him attempt to auction the case off to the highest bidder would make for some hilarious segments, especially if someone unexpected ends up getting the case in the end.

Or, Danhausen could place a curse on the case so that whoever tried to cash it in fails miserably. There are multiple options for how to make this work.

This might not be the kind of decision every fan would enjoy, but if you like Danhausen, you would probably enjoy him running around with the briefcase for a while.

articles.title: Bayley Fuels WWE Rumors, New Reports on Joe Hendry and Ilja Dragunov's Exit amid AEW Buzz
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Bayley Has Exchange with Pearce Amid WWE Absence

ESPN Addresses 'Completely False' Rumors About Future WWE Contract

Bayley has not been seen on WWE programming since last month, but she got fans talking Sunday after an exchange with Raw general manager Adam Pearce.

In response to an Instagram post (h/t Derek Holloway of Ringside News) by Bayley about her 10-year anniversary of getting called up to WWE's main roster, Pearce commented with clapping hands emojis.

Bayley responded by writing, "Hey, let's talk," to which Pearce replied, "You know where to find me."

The last time Bayley appeared on a televised WWE show was on July 18 when she lost to Lyra Valkyria at Saturday Night's Main Event.

She subsequently had two matches at WWE live events, but it has now been over a month since Bayley was part of WWE programming.

Bayley's absence comes amid a great deal of speculation regarding her pro wrestling future.

While the exact end date of Bayley's WWE contract is not publicly known, Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer Radio (h/t WrestlingInc.com's Julien D'Alessandro ) reported earlier this month that he had heard her deal is up in January.

As is the case with any big WWE name who may be on the verge of free agency, some have theorized that Bayley could make the jump to AEW to reunite with longtime friend Mercedes Moné.

However, since Bayley's name has been mentioned often on WWE programming as of late, particularly by Valkyria, there is at least some belief that her WWE tenure may not be over yet.

Dave Meltzer of Wrestling Observer Radio (h/t Holloway ) recently offered his perspective, saying, "The frequent mentions of her on Raw this week would indicate to me that they expect her back. If they believed she might be leaving, they would not mention her name."

Bayley's exchange with Pearce could potentially be another clue that a return to WWE programming is possible, but anything could be on the table until and unless she resurfaces.

Reported Reason for Hendry's Recent WWE Hiatus

Joe Hendry's absence from WWE programming over the past few weeks is reportedly due to an outside-the-ring project he is working on for the company.

According to PWInsider.com (h/t Felix Upton of Ringside News), Hendry has a role in a live-action micro-drama for mobile platforms as part of WWE's partnership with ReelShort.

Prior to his hiatus, Hendry took part in a concert with Danhausen on the July 27 episode of Raw. However, they were interrupted and attacked by Judgment Day members Dominik Mysterio and JD McDonagh, as well as boxer Ryan Garcia.

At SummerSlam, Hendry showed up during the Human Monies on a Pole match between Danhausen and Mysterio, and he helped Danhausen pull off the victory.

The next night on Raw, Hendry lost decisively in a match against Bron Breakker, and he has not shown up on Raw since then.

Hendry was called up to WWE's main roster in April following a successful run in NXT that saw him hold the NXT Championship once.

While Hendry has not enjoyed that same level of success on Raw yet, the fact that WWE is using him for outside projects suggests that the company sees plenty of value in his skill set.

Rumors on Dragunov's Future After WWE Departure

Ilja Dragunov is reportedly being linked to AEW following the expiration of his WWE contract.

According to Fightful Select (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News), AEW sources have not yet heard about Dragunov joining the company, but other sources within pro wrestling expressed their belief that Dragunov ultimately will sign with AEW based on a "hunch."

PWInsider.com (h/t WrestlePurists ) first reported Saturday that Dragunov's WWE contract was expiring, leading to his exit from the company.

False Finish followed up by reporting that although WWE "would have liked Dragunov to stay with the company," he ultimately made the decision to leave.

Given that Dragunov's contract expired rather than him getting notified of a release, the typical 90-day non-compete clause does not apply to him.

That means Dragunov is a free agent and already free to work elsewhere at any time.

The 32-year-old Dragunov has long been regarded as one of the most physical and entertaining in-ring workers in pro wrestling, which led to some major accolades in WWE.

Dragunov was both an NXT United Kingdom and NXT champion before getting called up to the main roster and holding the United States Championship.

However, Dragunov's screen time took a major hit after he dropped the U.S. title to Carmelo Hayes in December, and he had not been seen on WWE programming since April prior to his departure.

If Dragunov and AEW do have mutual interest, it would perhaps behoove them to get a deal done quickly because he could show up next Sunday at the All In pay-per-view as a surprise entrant in the Casino Gauntlet match.

articles.title: Cambuur fans suffer burns as fireworks set off during Dutch league match
articles.summary: Game resumed despite injuries to home fans, but it would have been abandoned if a player or match official had been hit.
articles.body:
Dutch side SC Cambuur has said fans suffered burns, hearing damage and eye injuries after visiting Feyenoord supporters threw fireworks during a league match in Leeuwarden in the Netherlands province of Friesland.

The match on Sunday was halted for about 20 minutes in the first half when fans in the away section lit large numbers of red flares and threw fireworks.

Some were aimed towards sections of the ground containing Cambuur supporters, while one exploded on the pitch just a few metres from Feyenoord goalkeeper Tjark Ernst.

“Our own goalkeeper had a flare fired at him and only just managed to avoid it,” said Feyenoord general manager Robert Eenhoorn, describing the incident as “simply terrible”.

Cambuur said in a statement on Monday that five fans were confirmed to have been injured and that the club would work with the authorities to make sure those responsible were caught.

“It should be clear that setting off and firing fireworks is completely unacceptable and has no place in a football stadium whatsoever,” the club added.

Leeuwarden Mayor Foort van Oosten also condemned the incident and promised an investigation, while the Dutch football association said it would revisit its protocols for incidents of disorder.

The game resumed despite the injuries to the supporters, but it would have been abandoned if a player or match official had been hit.

“That doesn’t feel right,” Jan Bluyssen, KNVB manager of professional football competition affairs, told Dutch news agency ANP.

“We need to examine whether the protocol is still appropriate and how we might want to adjust it.”

Feyenoord won the match 5-2 to maintain their unbeaten start to the new league season, while newly promoted Cambuur have lost all three of their opening matches.

England fast bowler ‌Brydon Carse has been dropped from the squad for the second ⁠Test against ⁠Pakistan amid an investigation into an incident at a club in Derby, the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) has said.

“Following a ⁠referral from the ECB, the Cricket Regulator has confirmed that they will investigate events on Saturday night in Derby,” the board said in a statement on Monday.

“Brydon ⁠Carse will no longer be available for selection for the second men’s test while this investigation is ongoing and the full facts are obtained.”

Carse, who did not play in the opening test victory at Headingley, will be replaced by Sonny ‌Baker.

Videos circulated on social media appearing to show the 31-year-old Durham bowler in handcuffs being spoken to by police officers outside a venue. According to reports, Carse was not arrested and no charges were brought.

It has been a busy summer for England’s Cricket Regulator, the body set up to investigate matters where there is an allegation of a breach of ⁠the ECB’s code of conduct.

In June, it concluded an ⁠investigation into former test captain Ben Stokes and fast bowler Gus Atkinson after a nightclub incident following the first test against New Zealand.

Both were left out of the second test before ⁠the regulator ruled that there was insufficient evidence to establish that any regulatory breach occurred.

The latest investigation comes five ⁠days after England’s returning test captain Joe Root ⁠spoke of the players being “really good role models and human beings” following a series of incidents and accusations of a drinking culture.

Controversy has followed England recently, with off-field issues ‌during last winter’s tours – including Harry Brook being fined 30,000 pounds ($41,000) following an altercation in Wellington, New Zealand – as well as reports of drinking during a mid-Ashes series trip ‌to ‌Noosa.

Stokes retired from international cricket after returning for the third test against New Zealand and Brendon McCullum was sacked as test coach.

articles.title: ‘Not everything was perfect': Bryson DeChambeau's curious LIV comments raise questions
articles.summary: Following LIV Golf's season finale, Bryson DeChambeau offered up some conflicting thoughts on the league's future that raised questions.
articles.body:
The dust is still settling from LIV Golf's 2026 season finale in Indianapolis . The question now is whether it will prove to be the final LIV Golf tournament in history. Bryson DeChambeau didn't provide much clarity on the matter Sunday night.

Instead, DeChambeau offered up conflicting thoughts on LIV's future, at first professing his excitement at "what could happen next year," before talking about LIV in the past tense and even acknowledging unspecified mistakes the upstart league has made.

DeChambeau after LIV's season finale: 'We did something different in the game'

After a year of increasingly bad news, LIV's season came to an abrupt end on Sunday night at LIV Golf Indianapolis.

With the season-ending Team Championship cancelled, both the season-long individual winner (Jon Rahm) and the 2026 team winner (Rahm's Legion XIII) were determined.

DeChambeau finished T3 in Indy , leaving him in second place in the final Individual standings, while his Crushers team failed to make the final podium.

With funding for the league gone, thanks to the PIF's decision to cut its losses earlier this year , no one knows if a 2027 LIV season will happen.

'We have a lot against us': Bryson DeChambeau gets real about LIV's uncertain future

While Phil Mickelson was the primary force behind the creation of LIV Golf, DeChambeau was always the league's biggest star and public booster. With the league's future in doubt, that remains the case… to a point.

Even after Sunday's round was over, DeChambeau was still expressing optimism for what the future holds for LIV, at least at first.

"I think there's a lot of potential moving forward. It's been an interesting ride, that's for sure," DeChambeau said Sunday night. "You know just as much as I have everything that we've gone through and the tough moments that we've had. But it's made us stronger."

He then invoked the concept of LIV 2.0, which the league's CEO hopes will be anchored by new big-money investors , and revealed he has "great thoughts" about next season without divulging any details.

"As much as we're transitioning from LIV 1.0 to 2.0, I have great thoughts about what could happen next year. I wish I could be more up front about it," DeChambeau said.

However, after his initial positivity, DeChambeau then switched to talking about LIV Golf in the past tense and alluded to mistakes the league made over the years.

"But ultimately I'm proud of the fact of what we've done, the good and some of the bad that we've unfortunately had, things that have occurred," DeChambeau said. "I'm going to be real with it; not everything was perfect. But for the most part we've done a solid job."

But his closing line should raise the most questions among observers and fans interested in what the future holds for LIV, if there is a future at all. Bryson again delivered it in the past tense.

"If there's one thing that I could say, it's we did something different in the game of golf, and I'm proud of that."

That sounds an awful lot like LIV's biggest proponent is resigned to the fact that the league might be finished for good.

articles.title: WWE Contracts, '90-Day No-Compete Clause' Finally Explained by Former Champion in New Video
articles.summary: WWE is rumored to be going through roster cuts sometime soon, and one wrestler who went through that experience shined some light on how things play out.
articles.body:
WWE is rumored to be going through roster cuts sometime soon, and one wrestler who went through that experience shined some light on how things play out.

Raj Dhesi, formerly known as one-time WWE Champion Jinder Mahal, resurfaced his video explaining why wrestlers are required to sit out for 90 days after being cut, even though "there is no such thing as a no-compete clause in WWE."

"When you sign a WWE contract, in the writing it states, 'WWE can terminate your contract with 90 days' notice.' So when you receive the phone call, it's them letting you know that in 90 days, your contract is cut," Dhesi explained. "They will pay you for the 90 days. That distinction is very important, because if it was a no-compete clause, you would not get paid for 90 days. For 90 days, you are still under WWE contract."

ESPN Addresses 'Completely False' Rumors About Future WWE Contract

Dhesi went on to add that wrestlers who are cut are pulled from live events and shows to protect both themselves and the company from future liabilities such as injuries or misrepresenting the brand in any way.

"In my opinion, WWE paying you for 90 days is an incredible gesture," Dhesi said. "It gives you time to reorganize your life. You're not making moves out of desperation or anger, and it actually protects both parties."

articles.title: A brief history of the RB1 in fantasy football scoring and the dreaded curse that follows the player year-to-year
articles.summary: It's been a tough run for the RB1 in fantasy football the season after their top performance. More from Joel Smyth.
articles.body:
The overall RB1 is the most important player in all of fantasy football. Analyst Joel Smyth goes over the curse of RB1s past, why the overall No. 1 player is so important for winning leagues and who they could be in 2026.

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Football league for the 2026 NFL season

Former RB1s of the season prior have not fared well the following season; some would even say they've been cursed. Whether it's injury or a steep decline, the player who dominated the league the year before, often being taken first overall, has failed to live up to expectations in each of the past seven seasons, with Alvin Kamara being the lone top RB exception (although still dipping by 7.0 PPG).

Below is a look at the RB1 from the past seven seasons in Full-PPR formats.

Christian McCaffrey will be up to bat for the third time on this list, with his first two seasons following an RB1 performance ending in season-long injuries that tanked fantasy teams. He's been the overall RB1 three times, making his 1.05 price tag seem plenty worth it, but his three season-killing years make it a terrifying selection at the same time.

To show just how bad the former RB1s have performed going back to 2015, comparing them to the top rookie back is shocking. Over the last 11 seasons, the No. 1 RB selected in the NFL Draft has outscored or performed the same as the former RB1 in PPG in nine of the 11 years. AKA, the Jeremiyah Love counterparts have done better or the same as the McCaffrey counterparts almost every season.

If you can find this year's overall RB1, the benefit cannot be overstated. If you draft the RB1, you win leagues. Last season, McCaffrey on your roster gave you a 25.7% chance of winning it all, up from your average ~8% chance in a 12-team league. Players that come extremely close have similar value as well, with Bijan Robinson being on 27.4% of championship teams because of his Week 17 blow-up. The elite RB upside is the key.

Over the last decade, the difference between the RB1 and an RB1 (the RB12), is incomparable. So much so that even if you combined the overall RB1 with the worst possible RB flex play (the RB36), it would still be more valuable to have than the RB12 + RB13 in nine of the 10 seasons, and not really close with a 4.1 PPG advantage for the RB1 + RB36.

Another great way to show the value gap is just in salary cap leagues. Analyst Justin Boone has Jahmyr Gibbs, the overall RB1 in ADP, valued at $57, while the RB12 Kyren Williams is way down at $24.

Fantasy Football: 3 big-name quarterbacks we're fading at ADP this season

Fantasy Football: Justin Boone's backup running back rankings for 2026

Fantasy Football Running Back Scouting Reports: A preview of some of the RB profiles in the Yahoo Fantasy Ultra Playbook

Historically, overall RB1s have not been found after Round 2, with only three since 2005 (14%) being selected outside the top-24, with the majority being Round 1 selections. That would narrow us down to 12 RBs.

Gibbs, the current 1.01 in ADP, is my easy selection for the best odds. In short, the Lions averaged over 31 RB fantasy PPG last season, even with an offensive coordinator firing mid-season. The current RB2 is an injured Isiah Pacheco, with Sione Vaki behind him with one touch in 2025. There is a shot he has LT or 2019 CMC-level upside this year.

Robinson and McCaffrey are the next tier behind. McCaffrey has zero issues outside of injury history and age risk, making him a great pick if your league does not have a last-place punishment. Robinson is nearly equal to Gibbs, just on a much lower offense, especially with their current QB room.

Of the later RB picks, there are three other names I think have a good shot. James Cook III is one, with the best combination of offense and offensive line; Cook is only his rumored receiving role away from another career year. Kenneth Walker III has the offense, talent and volume potential to make it happen in Round 2, with an injury scare moving him back in drafts. The goal line and receiving potential as the best offensive skill player on the team makes for a huge opportunity.

Last, I'd give Omarion Hampton a shoutout. If Keaton Mitchell is nothing more than the RB2 he's been in the past, Hampton finds himself in an amazing RB offense with all the goal-line work on a good team. His receiving chops, which we saw in his rookie season, can propel him to the classic second-year ceiling season that we've seen in recent years for players like Robinson, Gibbs, Breece Hall and Jonathan Taylor.
